lines.text: Every part is designed to be made.
But not every detail is meant to be simulated.
Fillets. Chamfers. Holes. A logo.
To a solver, each one is noise. Thousands of extra elements. Hours of compute you'll never get back.
So we built something that knows the difference.
This is DeFeat.
It reads the exact geometry of your part, and recognizes every feature. Rules and a neural network, trained on real-world cad.
Tell it the analysis. Static, modal, thermal, or flow. It decides what matters.
Then it removes the rest. Cleanly. Without ever breaking the solid.
And it doesn't ask for your trust. It earns it.
Both models are meshed and solved, side by side. If the stress shifts too far, the right features come back. Automatically.
Fifty-five percent fewer elements. Under three percent change in deflection.
Open source. Private by design. It runs entirely on your machine.
DeFeat. Simulation-ready, by design.
This is DeFeat, from a raw cad file to a model that's ready to simulate. Eight short steps. Let's begin.
First, install it. Clone the repository and run the setup script. It brings everything with it: the geometry kernel, the mesher, the solver, and the neural network.
On Windows, use the PowerShell script instead. Then start the app, and open your browser.
Drop in a step file, or simply describe a part in plain English.
Or start from a sample. Every card previews what's about to change.
DeFeat reads the boundary representation and finds every feature. Each one comes with a plain-English reason, and a second opinion from the neural network.
Click a chip to isolate a class. Bright faces will be removed. Faded ones stay.
Now choose your analysis. Static, modal, thermal, or flow.
Set the mesh size. Anything smaller than the threshold is marked for removal, while ribs and load paths are kept.
Press Simplify. Removal runs in a guarded worker, so a difficult face can never take the app down.
Then both models are meshed and solved. You see the element count, the change in volume, and the shift in deflection.
If simplifying moves the result by more than five percent, the stress guard restores the features that matter. On its own.
Drag across to compare before and after.
When you're happy, export the simplified step file, a full report, and Python or C plus plus code that reproduces every step.
Prefer to just ask? The assistant runs locally, and turns your words into exact actions you can see.
Or press Command K, and do anything from the keyboard.
For a whole folder of parts, run it from the command line. And if you live in FreeCAD, there's a macro for that too.
Every number is measured on held-out, real-world cad. Fillets found with an F1 of zero point eight four. And a valid solid, every single time.
DeFeat. Step in. Simulation-ready step out. Proven.
